related_links.title: Thursday Games To Watch: Tupelo and Lake Cormorant

article.headline: Scores from last Night: Lake Cormorant finishes perfect; Tupelo shuts out DeSoto Central
article.html:
Lake Cormorant completed a perfect 10-0 regular season, Tupelo reached 11-0 with a shutout, and several football games came down to a single possession Thursday, November 5. The Gators won 42-14 at Olive Branch, while the Golden Wave beat visiting DeSoto Central 38-0.

Elsewhere, Meridian defeated Brandon 40-34 and Starkville beat Oxford 55-28. Center Hill and Pontotoc each escaped with one-point road wins, and Petal needed overtime to get past Northwest Rankin. Those finishes led a night that also brought close basketball games and unbeaten starts extended in soccer.

Football: Lake Cormorant finishes perfect; Tupelo adds a shutout

Lake Cormorant turned its opportunity for a perfect regular season into a 42-14 win at Olive Branch. The Gators finished 10-0, with the Conquistadors listed at 3-8 after the loss. DeSoto County News confirms the unbeaten regular-season finish, a concrete milestone before attention shifts to the postseason.

Tupelo kept DeSoto Central off the scoreboard in a 38-0 home win. The result left the Golden Wave 11-0 and the Jaguars 7-3. Tupelo and Lake Cormorant were among the teams followed in our Thursday Games To Watch preview.

Football: Meridian and Starkville win region matchups

Meridian beat Brandon 40-34 at home, leaving both teams listed at 7-3. The Wildcats outscored the Bulldogs 14-7 in the fourth quarter of the six-point win.

Starkville defeated visiting Oxford 55-28. The Yellowjackets moved to 7-3, while the Chargers were listed at 8-2 afterward. Starkville carries that decisive result into the postseason.

Football: one-point wins and an overtime finish

Center Hill edged South Panola 30-29 in Batesville. The Mustangs outscored the Tigers 13-7 in the fourth quarter to finish 8-2; South Panola was listed at 5-4. The final period supplied the difference in the narrow road victory.

Pontotoc won 49-48 at Lafayette, moving to 8-2 while the Commodores stood at 8-3. The Warriors scored 21 points in the fourth quarter and Lafayette scored 20, keeping the teams separated by the smallest possible margin at the finish.

Petal beat Northwest Rankin 48-45 in overtime. The Panthers outscored the Cougars 21-7 in the fourth quarter and 6-3 in the extra period, finishing 9-2. Northwest Rankin was listed at 3-7.

Football: Hernando wins; Horn Lake answers an early deficit

Hernando won 31-14 at Southaven to reach 7-3, with the Chargers at 2-7. Horn Lake defeated visiting Lewisburg 50-14 after trailing 14-0 at the end of the first quarter. The Eagles scored 50 unanswered points over the remaining quarters and finished 2-8; Lewisburg was listed at 3-7.

The MHSAA Class 7A bracket page links to the posted championship bracket, which lists the first round for November 13. Its pairings and higher-seed hosting rule put Starkville at Tupelo, Horn Lake at Oxford, Brandon at Gulfport, and St. Martin at Meridian.

Basketball: North Pontotoc wins by one; Yazoo City and Warren Central split

North Pontotoc boys held the one-point edge in a 55-54 win at Mooreville. The Vikings remained unbeaten at 2-0, while the Troopers were listed at 1-1.

Warren Central boys beat Yazoo City 61-53 in Vicksburg to reach 4-0; the Indians fell to 1-1. The girls result went the other way: Yazoo City won 47-42, keeping the Indians unbeaten at 2-0 and leaving Warren Central at 2-2.

Soccer: Saltillo stays perfect; Hernando sweeps shutouts

Saltillo girls won 2-1 over Itawamba Agricultural, extending their start to 4-0. The Tigers scored once in each half, while the Indians scored in the second half and finished 3-1. It was the first loss listed for Itawamba Agricultural.

Hernando kept Olive Branch off the scoreboard in both soccer games. The boys won 3-0 and were listed at 4-0, with Olive Branch at 1-2. The girls won 7-0, leaving Hernando unbeaten at 3-0-1 and Olive Branch at 2-1.

Enterprise and West Lauderdale split in Collinsville. Enterprise boys won 3-2 and were listed at 1-2, while the Knights stood at 3-2. West Lauderdale girls won 5-0, scoring four goals before halftime and one afterward to reach 3-0; Enterprise was listed at 2-1.
